# AIEF-ARCH-001 — AI Engineering Framework: Architecture Specification

**Framework:** AIEF — AI Engineering Framework
**Document:** AIEF-ARCH-001
**Revision:** A — ARCHITECTURE FREEZE CANDIDATE
**Date:** 2026-08-07
**Author:** Chief AI Systems Architect
**Status:** Design only. No framework files are generated by this document.

---

## 0. Scope and Constraints

This document specifies the **complete architecture** of a reusable `.ai/` directory that governs AI-assisted engineering projects. It is a design specification, not an implementation.

| In scope | Out of scope |
|---|---|
| Directory architecture and file specification | File contents, templates, prompts, law texts |
| Context loading and precedence model | Any SEWCP-specific content |
| Agent registry contracts | Runtime implementation for any specific host |
| Engineering law taxonomy | Model selection or tuning |
| Workflow and lifecycle state machines | CI script implementation |
| Versioning and upgrade semantics | — |

**SEWCP is the first instance, not the subject.** Nothing in this architecture may encode semiconductor-specific, mechanical-specific, or CAD-specific assumptions.

---

## 1. The Design Problem

Six failure modes make AI-assisted engineering unreliable. The architecture is a direct response to each.

| # | Failure mode | Architectural response |
|---|---|---|
| **F1** | **Context death.** Sessions are stateless. The model forgets everything between invocations. | Repository-resident state (`STATE.md`) written at session end, read at session start. Memory is never the carrier. |
| **F2** | **Silent drift.** The model asserts a state that does not exist, or resolves ambiguity by assumption. | Stop-condition law + machine-verified freeze registry with content hashes. |
| **F3** | **Model lock-in.** Frameworks built on one vendor's tool semantics die when the vendor changes. | Agents are **contracts**, not runtime objects. Host specifics isolated in a thin adapter layer. |
| **F4** | **Context budget exhaustion.** Loading everything at boot leaves no room to work, and fails outright on small-context models. | Five-tier lazy loading with a hard boot budget. |
| **F5** | **Authority collapse.** When instructions conflict, the model picks arbitrarily. | Explicit, total precedence ordering with AI inference ranked last. |
| **F6** | **Unupgradeable frameworks.** Project data and framework data intermingle, so the framework can never be updated. | Hard `core/` versus `project/` partition with wholesale-replacement semantics. |

> **The governing insight:** an AI engineering framework is not documentation. It is an **operating system** — a bootloader, a state machine, a scheduler, a policy kernel, and a filesystem contract. Documentation describes; an OS constrains.

---

## 2. Architectural Principles

The nine given principles are restated as enforceable architectural properties.

| # | Principle | Architectural property |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Repository is the source of truth | No decision exists unless it is a committed file. Conversation is not a record. |
| P2 | AI memory is never trusted | Every session boots cold from disk. State claims are verified against the ledger before use. |
| P3 | Every session is restartable | Session is a transaction: BEGIN reads state, COMMIT writes state + ledger. Abandonment rolls back cleanly. |
| P4 | Every decision is traceable | Append-only ledger; every artifact cites its authority; every approval binds a content hash. |
| P5 | Every change follows a workflow | Workflows are state machines with entry/exit criteria, not suggestions. |
| P6 | Architecture freezes are respected | Frozen artifacts are hash-registered and CI-verified. Freeze violation is a build failure. |
| P7 | AI assists, never replaces judgement | AI inference is the **lowest** precedence rank. It can never override a law, a freeze, or a human. |
| P8 | Human approval for architecture change | Approval is an artifact with a content hash, not a remembered assent. |
| P9 | All work reproducible | Every output declares its inputs, framework version, and authority chain. |

---

## 3. Top-Level Architecture

### 3.1 The Three-Partition Model

The single most important structural decision. Analogous to `/usr` (vendor), `/etc` (local config), `/var` (runtime data).

```
.ai/
├── BOOT.md            ← single entry point, host-independent
├── FRAMEWORK.md       ← identity, version, compatibility contract
├── README.md          ← human orientation (never read by agents)
│
├── core/              ← FRAMEWORK PARTITION
│                        Identical in every repository using this version.
│                        READ-ONLY to projects. Replaced wholesale on upgrade.
│                        Contains: laws, agents, workflows, lifecycle,
│                        templates, schemas, validation.
│
├── project/           ← INSTANCE PARTITION
│                        Unique to this repository. NEVER overwritten by an
│                        upgrade. Contains: binding, state, freeze registry,
│                        roster, gates, tasks, approvals, ECRs, sessions, ledger.
│
└── adapters/          ← HOST PARTITION
                         Maps framework concepts onto a specific AI host.
                         Swappable. Additive. One file per host.
```

**Upgrade semantics** follow directly: `rm -rf .ai/core && cp -r <new>/core .ai/core`. Nothing in `project/` is at risk. Adapters are merged, not replaced.

**Write permissions are architectural, not advisory:**

| Partition | Agents may write? | Human may write? | Upgrade replaces? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `core/` | **Never** | Only to author a new framework version | **Yes, wholesale** |
| `project/` | Yes, per law | Yes | **Never** |
| `adapters/` | Never | Yes | Merge only |

### 3.2 Naming and Identification

| Element | Scheme | Example form |
|---|---|---|
| Framework | `AIEF` | — |
| Framework version | `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` | Semantic; MAJOR = breaking contract change |
| Laws | `LAW-nn` | 01–12 |
| Agents | `AGT-<role-slug>` | Stable slug, human-readable |
| Workflows | `WF-nn` | 01–06 |
| Lifecycle stages | `LC-nn` | 01–10 |
| Templates | `TPL-<slug>` | — |
| Schemas | `SCH-<slug>` | — |
| Sessions | `S-<ISO8601>-<seq>` | Monotonic |
| Ledger entries | `L-<seq>` | Strictly monotonic, never reused |
| Tasks | `T-<seq>` | — |
| ECRs | `ECR-<class>-<seq>` | Class ∈ {Q, D} |
| Approvals | `APR-<seq>` | — |

## 4. Context Loading Architecture

### 4.1 Five-Tier Model

Loading everything is the default failure. Tiers bound the cost of being oriented.

| Tier | Name | Trigger | Budget | Contents |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **T0** | Entry | Always, first action | ≤ 400 tok | `BOOT.md` only |
| **T1** | Orientation | Always | ≤ 3,500 tok | `FRAMEWORK.md`, `project/STATE.md`, `project/BINDING.md`, `core/laws/INDEX.md`, `core/PRECEDENCE.md` |
| **T2** | Role | On role assignment | ≤ 2,500 tok | `core/agents/<role>` spec, `core/agents/AGENT-CONTRACT`, laws flagged binding for that role |
| **T3** | Task | On task acceptance | ≤ 6,000 tok | `project/tasks/<id>`, relevant template, relevant workflow, cited source artifacts |
| **T4** | Deep | Explicit request only | Unbounded | Ledger history, archived sessions, superseded artifacts, full law texts |

> **Hard requirement: T0 + T1 ≤ 4,000 tokens.** This is the portability constraint. A model that cannot afford 4k tokens to become oriented cannot run engineering work at all. Every framework file's size budget in §5 derives from this ceiling.

**Tier discipline is a law (LAW-09).** An agent that loads T4 without cause is burning the budget that verification needs.

### 4.2 Boot Sequence

Deterministic and ordered. Not "read the documentation."

| Step | Action | Failure behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | Read `BOOT.md` | If absent → framework not installed; halt |
| B2 | Read `FRAMEWORK.md`; compare framework version to `project/BINDING.md` pin | Incompatible → **HALT**, require human upgrade decision |
| B3 | Read `project/STATE.md` | Absent → uninitialised project; enter Lifecycle LC-01 |
| B4 | **Staleness check:** compare `STATE.last_ledger_seq` to highest sequence in ledger | Mismatch → **HALT**. State diverged from history; human reconciliation required |
| B5 | Read `project/BINDING.md` — lifecycle stage, active gate, approval authority | — |
| B6 | Read `core/laws/INDEX.md` and `core/PRECEDENCE.md` | — |
| B7 | Read `project/OPEN_ITEMS.md` — blockers, open ECRs, pending approvals | — |
| B8 | Declare: framework version, lifecycle stage, active gate, blockers, proposed next action | — |
| B9 | **Await role assignment.** Do not act. | — |

**B4 is the anti-drift mechanism.** It is the structural answer to a model asserting a state that does not exist: state and history must reconcile arithmetically or work does not begin.

**B9 is the anti-autonomy mechanism.** Booting produces orientation, never action.

### 4.3 Precedence Hierarchy

Total ordering. Every conflict resolves by rank. No tie-breaking judgement.

| Rank | Authority | Overrides |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | Live human instruction in session | Everything below |
| **2** | Recorded human approval (`project/approvals/`) | 3–7 |
| **3** | Freeze registry (`project/FROZEN.md`) | 4–7 |
| **4** | Engineering laws (`core/laws/`) | 5–7 |
| **5** | Project binding (`project/BINDING.md`) | 6–7 |
| **6** | Agent specification (`core/agents/`) | 7 |
| **7** | **AI inference and judgement** | **Nothing** |

> Rank 7 is the encoding of principle P7. An AI conclusion — however well-reasoned — cannot override a law, a freeze, an approval, or a human. It may **raise an ECR** against any of them. That is its only path to changing a higher rank.

**Rank 1 above rank 3 is deliberate and load-bearing.** A human may override a freeze verbally, but the override must be recorded as an approval artifact before dependent work is committed, or the session cannot close (LAW-10).

**Owner** = the role accountable for correctness. **Size** = target; ceiling in parentheses where a budget binds.

| File | Purpose | Responsibilities | Read when | Updated when | Dependencies | Size | Owner | Lifecycle |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BOOT.md` | Single entry point | Declare boot sequence B1–B9; point to tiers; forbid action before role assignment | **T0, every session, first** | Framework upgrade only | None (must be self-contained) | 40–60 ln (≤400 tok) | Chief Systems Engineer | Framework-versioned; immutable per version |
| `FRAMEWORK.md` | Framework identity | Version; compatibility contract; partition rules; glossary; write-permission matrix | T1 | Framework upgrade | `core/VERSION` | 120–180 ln | Chief Systems Engineer | Framework-versioned |

|---|---|---|---|
| T0 | 1 | ≤400 tok | — |
| T1 | 7 | ≤3,500 tok | **Boot ceiling = 3,900 tok ✔** |

> **Only 8 of 80 files are read at boot.** That ratio is the architecture working: a large, complete framework with a small, bounded entry cost.

---

## 6. Workflow Architecture

Twelve phases, six workflow files, one state machine.

```
        ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │                    SESSION SCOPE                     │
        │                                                      │
  ①SESSION START ──▶ ②CONTEXT LOADING ──▶ ③AGENT CREATION      │
        │                                        │             │
        │                                        ▼             │
        │                                 ④TASK EXECUTION      │
        │                                        │             │
        │              ┌─────────────────────────┤             │
        │              ▼                         ▼             │
        │      ⑤ENGINEERING REVIEW ──────▶ ⑥DESIGN REVIEW      │
        │              │                         │             │
        │              │    ┌────────────────────┘             │
        │              ▼    ▼                                  │
        │        ⑦IMPLEMENTATION ──▶ ⑧VERIFICATION             │
        │                                   │                  │
        │                    ┌──────────────┤                  │
        │                    ▼              ▼                  │
        │              ⑨GIT COMMIT ──▶ ⑩RELEASE                │
        │                    │                                 │
        │                    ▼                                 │
        │              ⑪SESSION END  ◀── mandatory             │
        └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                             │
                             ▼
                    ⑫PROJECT CLOSEOUT (terminal, once)
```

### 6.1 Phase Specification

| # | Phase | Workflow | Entry | Exit | Produces | Blocking condition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ① | Session Start | WF-01 | Any invocation | B1–B9 complete; orientation declared | Session ID; ledger BEGIN | Staleness (B4) → halt |
| ② | Context Loading | WF-01 | Orientation declared | Required tiers loaded and declared | Tier declaration | Tier budget exceeded → escalate |
| ③ | Agent Creation | WF-02 | Task exists | Role assigned; T2 loaded; contract acknowledged | Role declaration | Separation-of-duty conflict → reassign |
| ④ | Task Execution | WF-02 | Role assigned; task package read | Deliverable meets template contract | Deliverable | LAW-12 stop condition → halt, raise ECR |
| ⑤ | Engineering Review | WF-03 | Deliverable exists | Technical correctness assessed | Review record | Originator = reviewer → reject |
| ⑥ | Design Review | WF-03 | Engineering review passed | Formal disposition recorded | Review record; actions | Action on critical path → gate fails |
| ⑦ | Implementation | WF-04 | Approved design | Artifact produced; traceability satisfied | Artifact + trace links | Frozen-artifact write → halt |
| ⑧ | Verification | WF-04 | Artifact exists | Binary pass/fail on every criterion | Verification report | Self-verification → invalid |
| ⑨ | Git Commit | WF-05 | Verification passed | Committed under LAW-07 | Commit | Attribution violation → reject |
| ⑩ | Release | WF-05 | Gate passed | Tagged; notes issued; ledger recorded | Tag + release notes | Open blocking ECR → no release |
| ⑪ | Session End | WF-01 | Any session termination | STATE written; ledger appended; handoff stated | STATE + summary + ledger COMMIT | **Cannot be skipped** |
| ⑫ | Project Closeout | WF-06 | Final gate passed | Archive sealed; state terminal | Closeout record | Open items → cannot close |

### 6.2 Session as Transaction

The most important operational semantic.

| DB concept | Framework equivalent |
|---|---|
| `BEGIN` | Boot B1–B9; ledger BEGIN entry |
| Working set | In-session context and edits |
| `COMMIT` | STATE.md rewritten + session summary filed + ledger entry appended, **atomically at close** |
| `ROLLBACK` | Session abandoned without close: STATE unchanged, no ledger entry. Repository remains consistent; uncommitted work is orphaned by design |
| Isolation | One active session per repository; concurrent sessions require explicit lock |

> **An abandoned session must leave the repository exactly as it found it.** This is what makes P3 (restartable) real: a crashed session is not a corrupt session.

### 6.3 Escalation Ladder

Uniform across all phases.

```
Agent detects condition
        │
        ├─ Clarification ──▶ log in session summary ──▶ proceed
        │
        ├─ Ambiguity ──────▶ raise ECR-Q ──▶ Chief Systems Engineer rules ──▶ proceed under ruling
        │
        ├─ Defect ─────────▶ STOP affected work ──▶ raise ECR-D ──▶ human disposition ──▶ re-gate
        │
        └─ Freeze conflict ▶ STOP ──▶ require human approval artifact ──▶ proceed or abandon
```

---

## 7. Agent Registry

### 7.1 Agent Model

> **An agent is a contract, not a runtime object.**

This single decision delivers model-agnosticism. The same specification is executable by: a host with native subagents (spawn one), a host without them (the model adopts the role serially and declares the switch), or a human. The contract — inputs, outputs, allowed, forbidden, escalation — is invariant across all three.

Every agent inherits from `AGENT-CONTRACT`: declare role on assumption, load T2, cite authority for every output, never exceed allowed actions, escalate rather than assume, hand off in writing.

### 7.2 Authority Levels

| Level | Meaning | Roles |
|---|---|---|
| **A0** | Advisory only; produces analysis, no artifacts of record | — |
| **A1** | Produces artifacts within an assigned task | Repository, CAD, Python, Documentation, Simulation, Manufacturing |
| **A2** | Verifies and may reject others' artifacts | QA |
| **A3** | Plans, gates, and allocates; cannot verify own plan | Project Manager |
| **A4** | Rules on ECRs; approves designs; cannot implement | Chief Systems Engineer |
| **H** | Human owner; sole authority for freeze/thaw and architecture change | — |

### 7.3 Separation of Duties — Structural Conflicts

| Constraint | Rationale |
|---|---|
| QA may never verify an artifact it produced | LAW-05; self-verification is not verification |
| A reviewer may never be the originator | LAW-04; the rule that has no exception |
| Project Manager may not gate-pass its own plan | Requires CSE or human concurrence |
| Chief Systems Engineer may not implement what it approved | Approval and production are separate acts |
| No agent may write `core/` | Framework is read-only to projects |
| No agent may write `project/FROZEN.md` or `project/approvals/` | Human authority only |

### 7.4 The Nine Roles

#### AGT-repository-engineer — A1

| Facet | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Responsibilities** | Version control; repository structure; migrations; branch and tag policy; release mechanics; `.gitignore` and ignore hygiene; commit and tag integrity |
| **Inputs** | Task package; LAW-07; LAW-01 freeze registry; release notes template; current tree state |
| **Outputs** | Commits; tags; release artifacts; structural migrations; repository reports |
| **Allowed** | Init/structure repositories; move files preserving content; author commits; apply annotated tags; create ignore rules; generate structure reports |
| **Forbidden** | Modify frozen artifact content; rewrite history (amend/rebase/force-push published refs); modify git author identity; add attribution or co-author trailers; move a tag; delete `project/ledger/` |
| **Escalation** | Freeze conflict → CSE. History-rewrite need → human. Structural change affecting other agents' outputs → PM. |

#### AGT-mechanical-cad-engineer — A1

| Facet | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Responsibilities** | Translate frozen specifications into CAD implementation packages, models, and drawings; parameter mastery; dimensional conformance |
| **Inputs** | Frozen specification set; parameter master; implementation package template; LAW-12 |
| **Outputs** | Implementation packages; models; drawings; conformance reports; ECRs against the specification |
| **Allowed** | Read the full specification set; author implementation packages; model within released dimensions; raise ECRs; declare HOLD on blocked features |
| **Forbidden** | Change any dimension; invent an interface; optimise a frozen design; resolve a specification ambiguity by assumption; proceed past a defect |
| **Escalation** | Ambiguity → ECR-Q to CSE. Contradiction or geometric impossibility → **STOP**, ECR-D, human. Missing dimension → ECR-D. |

> This role's forbidden list is deliberately the most restrictive in the registry. It is the role most tempted to improve what it is implementing, and the one where a silent assumption propagates furthest downstream.

#### AGT-python-engineer — A1

| Facet | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Responsibilities** | Framework tooling; validators; calculation libraries; schema enforcement; CI checks; automation |
| **Inputs** | Task package; schemas; validation manifest; LAW-05 |
| **Outputs** | Source modules; tests; validators; CI configuration; back-validation reports |
| **Allowed** | Author and test code; implement schema validation; automate checks; refactor own code |
| **Forbidden** | Encode an engineering value not traceable to a specification; write a validator that weakens a law; self-certify test adequacy; commit failing CI |
| **Escalation** | Law not machine-checkable as written → CSE. Calculation disagrees with specification → ECR-D. |

#### AGT-documentation-engineer — A1

| Facet | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Responsibilities** | Document numbering, indexing, reachability, dependency mapping, traceability matrices, maturity states |
| **Inputs** | All documents; LAW-06; LAW-08 |
| **Outputs** | Indexes; dependency maps; traceability matrices; reachability and numbering audits |
| **Allowed** | Read all documents; create indexes and maps; report defects; assign document numbers |
| **Forbidden** | **Modify document content** (structural moves only, with content preserved); interpret engineering content; resolve a numbering conflict affecting a frozen document without an ECR |
| **Escalation** | Numbering collision in frozen set → ECR-D. Orphan document → PM. Broken authority chain → CSE. |

#### AGT-qa-engineer — A2

| Facet | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Responsibilities** | Independent verification; audit; readiness reports; evidence sufficiency; defect reporting |
| **Inputs** | Artifact under audit; acceptance criteria; LAW-05; validation manifest |
| **Outputs** | Verification reports; readiness reports; findings with severity; pass/fail dispositions |
| **Allowed** | Read everything; execute read-only checks; reject artifacts; assign finding severity; demand re-verification |
| **Forbidden** | **Verify anything it produced**; modify the artifact under audit; interpret engineering intent; soften a finding without disposition; pass on partial evidence |
| **Escalation** | Blocking finding → PM + originating agent. Repeat finding → CSE. Unverifiable criterion → CSE for criterion revision. |

> QA is the only A2 role, and its independence is structural rather than behavioural. In hosts with subagents it runs as a separate agent; in hosts without, it must run as a separate session with a cold context. **Independence is a property of the context, not of the intent.**

#### AGT-simulation-engineer — A1

| Facet | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Responsibilities** | Analysis and simulation; model correlation; margin reporting; assumption declaration |
| **Inputs** | Frozen specification; models; load cases; LAW-05 |
| **Outputs** | Analysis reports; correlation studies; margin summaries; assumption registers |
| **Allowed** | Build analysis models; run studies; report margins; declare fidelity limits |
| **Forbidden** | Change design to make analysis converge; report results without stating assumptions and fidelity; substitute simulation for required physical verification; suppress a non-closing budget |
| **Escalation** | Budget fails to close → **STOP**, ECR-D, CSE + human. Fidelity insufficient → declare and escalate rather than qualify silently. |

#### AGT-manufacturing-engineer — A1

| Facet | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Responsibilities** | Producibility review; process selection; supplier capability; inspection planning; RFQ packaging |
| **Inputs** | Released drawings; specification; material and finish callouts |
| **Outputs** | RFQ packages; capability matrices; inspection plans; producibility findings; long-lead registers |
| **Allowed** | Assess producibility; select processes within specification; author inspection plans; assemble supplier packages |
| **Forbidden** | Relax a tolerance or finish for producibility; substitute a material; alter a drawing; commit to a supplier |
| **Escalation** | Unproducible as specified → ECR-D. Tolerance economically infeasible → ECR-Q with cost evidence. |

#### AGT-project-manager — A3

| Facet | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Responsibilities** | Planning; WBS; scheduling; gate administration; risk register; task allocation; dashboard |
| **Inputs** | Specification scope; roster; gate definitions; state; open items |
| **Outputs** | Plans; task packages; gate records; risk register; dashboards; status |
| **Allowed** | Create and allocate tasks; schedule; administer gates; maintain risk; declare blockers; re-sequence work |
| **Forbidden** | Make engineering decisions; change scope without approval; pass a gate on its own plan unaided; suppress a risk; assign an agent into a duty conflict |
| **Escalation** | Gate criteria unmet → fail the gate. Scope change → human. Resource conflict → human. |

#### AGT-chief-systems-engineer — A4

| Facet | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Responsibilities** | Technical authority; ECR disposition; design review chairing; architecture integrity; framework conformance |
| **Inputs** | ECRs; review packages; freeze registry; laws; precedence |
| **Outputs** | ECR rulings; review dispositions; approval recommendations; architecture decisions |
| **Allowed** | Rule on ECR-Q; recommend on ECR-D; chair reviews; interpret laws; halt work on integrity grounds |
| **Forbidden** | Approve a freeze change (human only); implement what it approved; overrule a human; rule on an ECR it raised |
| **Escalation** | Freeze change → **human, always**. Law inadequate → framework MAJOR proposal. Conflict between laws → human. |

## 8. Engineering Laws

Twelve laws. Ten were specified; two are additions justified below.

| ID | Law | Governs | Machine-checkable | Binding on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LAW-01 | Architecture Freeze | Freeze registry; hash verification; thaw procedure | **Fully** — hash comparison | All |
| LAW-02 | Engineering Change Request | ECR classes, raising, disposition, closure | Partially — schema + open-count | All |
| LAW-03 | Release Gates | Gate criteria, binary disposition, no deferral | Partially — criteria completeness | PM, CSE |
| LAW-04 | Design Review | Review classes; checker ≠ originator; quorum | **Fully** — originator/reviewer identity | CSE, QA, all A1 |
| LAW-05 | Verification & Reproducibility | Evidence classes; binarity; self-verification ban; reproducibility declaration | **Fully** — identity + evidence presence | QA, Simulation |
| LAW-06 | Traceability | Authority citation; requirement→verification mapping; no orphans | **Fully** — link resolution | Documentation, all |
| LAW-07 | Git & Configuration Control | Commit contract; tags; **attribution prohibitions**; author immutability; no history rewrite | **Fully** — message and identity scan | Repository |
| LAW-08 | Documentation | Numbering; maturity states; sign-off; reachability | **Fully** — numbering and reachability | Documentation |
| LAW-09 | Session | Transaction semantics; tier discipline; mandatory close | Partially — state/ledger reconciliation | All |
| LAW-10 | Human Approval | Approval-as-artifact; hash binding; expiry; verbal-then-record | **Fully** — hash match | CSE, human |
| **LAW-11** | **Agent Conduct** | Role boundaries; separation of duties; escalation; impersonation ban | Partially — role declaration presence | All |
| **LAW-12** | **Ambiguity & Stop Conditions** | Finding taxonomy; **assumption prohibition**; stop triggers; Open Questions duty | Partially — Open Questions presence | All |

### 8.1 Why LAW-11 and LAW-12 Were Added

**LAW-11 (Agent Conduct)** — without it the agent registry is descriptive rather than binding. Forbidden-action lists need a law that makes violating them a defect rather than a stylistic lapse, and separation of duties needs an enforcement authority.

**LAW-12 (Ambiguity & Stop Conditions)** — the highest-value law in the set. Every other law governs what to do when the inputs are sound. LAW-12 governs the case that actually destroys engineering work: inputs that are **contradictory, incomplete, or impossible**, where the model's default behaviour is to smooth over the gap and proceed. It defines three finding classes, prohibits assumption as a resolution method, and makes "produce an Open Questions section and stop" a compliant deliverable rather than a failure to deliver.

### 8.2 Cross-Cutting Doctrines

Each law file specifies its own rules; these three properties span the set.

| Doctrine | Statement |
|---|---|
| **Hash binding** | Freezes and approvals bind a content hash. An approval that does not name what it approved is void. This defeats approval drift. |
| **Binary disposition** | Gates, verifications, and reviews produce pass or fail. "Substantially complete" is not a disposition. |
| **Evidence over assertion** | A claim in a document is not evidence for itself. Verification must cite an observation independent of the claim. |

---

## 9. Template Library

A template is an **output contract**: a producer's obligation and a consumer's guarantee.

| Template | Contract enforces | Producer | Consumer | Required elements |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Implementation Package | Traceability of every feature to a frozen source | Discipline engineer | Reviewer, implementer | Traceability matrix; parameters; sequence; verification checklist; **Open Questions**; release gate |
| Design Review | Reviewer ≠ originator; binary disposition | Reviewer | PM, CSE | Scope; criteria; findings with severity; disposition; actions with owners |
| Engineering Change Request | Classification and evidence before disposition | Any agent | CSE, human | Class (Q/D); affected artifacts; evidence; impact; requested action; disposition block |
| Session Summary | Continuity across context death | Session closer | Next session | Session ID; role; work performed; artifacts touched; decisions; open items; **explicit next action** |
| Verification Report | Independence and binarity | QA, Simulation | PM, gate | Criteria; method; evidence; per-criterion pass/fail; independence declaration |
| Release Notes | Reproducibility of a release | Repository Engineer | Human, downstream | Version; tag; contents; integrity statement; known open items |
| Issue Report | Actionability | Any agent | PM | Description; severity; reproduction; affected artifacts; proposed disposition |
| Agent Specification | Registry conformance | CSE | Framework | Responsibilities; inputs; outputs; allowed; forbidden; escalation; authority level |
| Task Package | Unambiguous assignment | PM | Assigned agent | Task ID; role; objective; inputs; deliverable; acceptance criteria; forbidden actions; escalation |
| Current State | Restartability | Session closer | Next session boot | Stage; gate; last ledger seq; blockers; active tasks; frozen hash; next action |

> Two templates carry disproportionate weight. **Session Summary** and **Current State** are the entire defence against context death — every other template documents work, these two make work resumable.

---

## 10. Project Lifecycle

Ten stages. Progression is gated; regression requires approval.

| # | Stage | Entry | Exit gate | Permitted agents | Key prohibition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LC-01 | Idea | Repository initialised | Concept recorded; scope bounded | PM, CSE | No implementation |
| LC-02 | Architecture | Concept approved | **Architecture freeze applied** | CSE, PM, Simulation | No detailed design |
| LC-03 | Specification | Architecture frozen | Specification set complete and frozen | CSE, discipline engineers | **No architecture change** |
| LC-04 | Implementation | Specification frozen | Artifacts complete and traced | All A1, PM | **No specification change** |
| LC-05 | Verification | Artifacts complete | All criteria binary-passed | QA, Simulation | **No self-verification** |
| LC-06 | Validation | Verification passed | Fitness for purpose demonstrated | QA, Manufacturing, CSE | No requirement revision to fit results |
| LC-07 | Release | Validation passed | Tagged, documented, published | Repository, PM | No release with open blocking ECR |
| LC-08 | Maintenance | Released | Steady state or revision triggered | All, on demand | No silent change |
| LC-09 | Revision | Change approved | New baseline frozen | CSE, PM, all | **Requires human approval to enter** |
| LC-10 | Archive | Project terminated | Archive sealed; state terminal | Repository, Documentation | **No further modification, ever** |

### 10.1 Transition Rules

| Rule | Statement |
|---|---|
| **Forward** | Only via a passed gate recorded in `project/GATES.md` |
| **Backward** | Only via human approval artifact; ledger records the regression and its cause |
| **Skip** | Prohibited without human approval; LC-05 Verification can never be skipped |
| **Re-entry** | LC-09 Revision re-enters LC-02 or LC-03 with a **new baseline version**; the prior baseline is superseded, never edited |
| **Terminal** | LC-10 is absorbing. Exiting requires creating a new project. |

### 10.2 Freeze Points

| Freeze | Applied at | Governs | Thaw |
|---|---|---|---|
| Architecture freeze | LC-02 exit | Structural decisions, interfaces, budgets | Human approval → LC-09 |
| Specification freeze | LC-03 exit | Dimensions, tolerances, materials, interfaces | Human approval → LC-09 |
| Design freeze | LC-04 exit | Released artifacts and drawings | ECR-D + human approval |
| Release freeze | LC-07 | Tagged release contents | Never — supersede with a new release |

---

## 11. Validation and Enforcement

A law enforced only by prose is a suggestion. The validation layer converts obligations into build failures.

| Check class | Verifies | Law | Failure |
|---|---|---|---|
| Freeze integrity | Content hash of every `FROZEN.md` entry matches the file | LAW-01 | **BLOCKING** |
| State reconciliation | `STATE.last_ledger_seq` equals ledger head | LAW-09 | **BLOCKING** |
| Ledger monotonicity | Sequence strictly increasing; no gaps, no rewrites | LAW-09 | **BLOCKING** |
| Approval binding | Every approval names a resolvable content hash | LAW-10 | **BLOCKING** |
| Commit hygiene | No forbidden attribution; no author modification; message conforms | LAW-07 | **BLOCKING** |
| Reviewer independence | Reviewer identity ≠ originator identity | LAW-04, LAW-05 | **BLOCKING** |
| Open ECR-D | No blocking ECR open at a gate or release | LAW-02, LAW-03 | **BLOCKING** |
| Schema conformance | State, task, ECR, approval, ledger records validate | LAW-08 | Blocking |
| Link resolution | Every relative link resolves | LAW-06 | Blocking |
| Numbering | No duplicate or missing document numbers | LAW-08 | Warning |
| Orphan detection | Every document reachable from the index | LAW-06 | Warning |
| Traceability coverage | Every requirement maps to a verification | LAW-06 | Warning at gate; blocking at release |

> **The validation layer runs without an LLM.** This is essential: enforcement that depends on a model's cooperation is not enforcement. Schemas and hashes are checkable by a script, in CI, deterministically.

---

## 12. Model Agnosticism

### 12.1 What Makes It Portable

| Design choice | Effect |
|---|---|
| Agents are contracts, not runtime objects | Executable by subagents, serial role adoption, or a human |
| No dependence on tool-calling semantics | Framework specifies *what* to read/write, never *how* |
| Plain-text files, no proprietary format | Any model that can read files can boot |
| Bounded boot budget (≤3,900 tok) | Runs on small-context models |
| Host specifics isolated in `adapters/` | New host = one new file, zero core changes |
| Validation is LLM-free | Enforcement survives model absence entirely |

### 12.2 Capability Degradation Ladder

The framework must function at every capability level, degrading in ceremony, never in discipline.

| Host capability | Adaptation | Discipline preserved? |
|---|---|---|
| Native subagents + tools + CI | Full: parallel agents, automated gates, CI enforcement | Fully |
| Tools, no subagents | Serial role adoption with declared switches; QA runs as a separate cold session | **Fully** — independence via context, not process |
| Chat only, no file access | Human mediates file I/O; boot by paste; agent produces file contents for human to commit | Fully, with human in the loop |
| No CI | Validation checks run manually at gates; results recorded as evidence | Fully, more slowly |

> **Discipline never degrades — only ceremony does.** A framework that requires a specific vendor's features to remain rigorous is not model-agnostic; it is that vendor's framework.

---

## 13. Framework Versioning and Upgrade

### 13.1 Semantics

| Increment | Meaning | Project action |
|---|---|---|
| **MAJOR** | Breaking contract change: law semantics, precedence, schema, partition layout | Explicit migration; human approval; ledger record |
| **MINOR** | Additive: new agent, new template, new check, new adapter | Adopt at convenience; backward compatible |
| **PATCH** | Clarification with no behavioural change | Adopt freely |

### 13.2 Compatibility Contract

`project/BINDING.md` pins a framework version range. Boot step B2 compares actual against pinned:

| Condition | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Within range | Proceed |
| Newer MINOR/PATCH | Proceed; note upgrade available |
| Newer MAJOR | **HALT.** Human migration decision required |
| Older than pinned | **HALT.** Framework downgrade is never silent |

### 13.3 Upgrade Procedure

1. Record intent in ledger.
2. Replace `core/` **wholesale**. Never merge.
3. Merge `adapters/` additively.
4. Leave `project/` **untouched**.
5. Run migration checks for the version delta.
6. Update the pin in `BINDING.md`.
7. Human approval artifact for MAJOR.
8. Ledger entry recording old → new version.

> Step 2 is why the partition exists. A framework that must be merged file-by-file will diverge across repositories within two upgrades, and the guarantee that every project runs the same laws is lost.

---

## 14. Failure Modes of the Framework Itself

Designing an OS requires anticipating how the OS fails.

| # | Failure mode | Consequence | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| FM-1 | **Ceremony exceeds value** — overhead per task discourages use, framework is bypassed | Silent abandonment; worst outcome, since discipline appears present | Bounded boot; tiered loading; ceremony proportional to lifecycle stage; LC-01/LC-08 deliberately light |
| FM-2 | **State/ledger divergence** | Corrupt continuity; work built on false premises | B4 staleness check is blocking; reconciliation requires a human |
| FM-3 | **Freeze registry rot** — hashes not updated after approved change | Freeze checks fail spuriously; team disables the check | Thaw procedure updates hashes atomically with the change; CI treats a stale hash as blocking, never as a warning |
| FM-4 | **Agent role bleed** — a role quietly exceeds its contract | Separation of duties collapses; self-verification returns | Mandatory role declaration; CI checks originator/reviewer identity; forbidden actions enumerated per role |
| FM-5 | **Template ossification** — templates outlive their usefulness, filled in ritually | Documents exist but carry no information | Templates specify *required information*, not required prose; MINOR versions retire unused templates |
| FM-6 | **Ledger unbounded growth** | Boot cost eventually breaches budget | Ledger is T4 only, never read at boot; periodic sealed archive with a hash chain |
| FM-7 | **Adapter drift** — host changes, adapter silently wrong | Boot misbehaves in host-specific ways | Adapters declare host version; boot warns on mismatch; generic adapter is always the fallback |
| FM-8 | **Law conflict** — two laws imply contradictory action | Agent paralysis or arbitrary choice | Precedence resolves rank conflicts; same-rank conflict escalates to human and triggers a MAJOR proposal |
| FM-9 | **Approval theatre** — approvals granted without reading | Human authority becomes a rubber stamp | Approval binds a content hash; approving requires naming what changed; expiry forces re-approval |
| FM-10 | **Bootstrap paradox** — framework governs its own development | Circular authority | Framework development is itself a project instance, governed by the **previous** framework version |

---

## 15. Adoption Path

SEWCP is the first instance and the proving ground.

| Step | Action | Validates |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Author `core/` at version 1.0.0 from this architecture | Completeness of the specification |
| 2 | Install `.ai/` into the SEWCP repository | Installation procedure |
| 3 | Initialise `project/` — binding, state, roster, gates | Instance partition sufficiency |
| 4 | **Retro-register the existing SEWCP freeze** in `FROZEN.md` with hashes | LAW-01 on a real frozen baseline |
| 5 | Migrate open ECRs into `project/ecr/` | LAW-02 against real defects |
| 6 | Run one full session cycle under WF-01 | Boot budget, transaction semantics, restartability |
| 7 | Run one QA cycle under LAW-05 with a cold context | Independence without subagents |
| 8 | Wire the validation manifest into CI | LLM-free enforcement |
| 9 | Extract every SEWCP-specific assumption that leaked into `core/` | **Reusability** |

> **Step 9 is the real test.** A framework proven on exactly one project is indistinguishable from that project's documentation. The framework is only reusable once a second, unlike project runs on it unchanged.

---

## 16. Open Design Decisions

These require ratification before the architecture is frozen. **No assumption has been made on any of them.**

| ID | Decision | Options | Impact if wrong |
|---|---|---|---|
| **OD-1** | Ledger format | Single append-only file · one file per entry · both with an index | File-per-entry scales but multiplies file count; single file risks merge conflicts under concurrency |
| **OD-2** | Hash algorithm and scope | SHA-256 of raw bytes · normalised content (line-ending agnostic) | Raw bytes will produce spurious freeze failures across OS line-ending differences |
| **OD-3** | Concurrency model | Single-session lock · optimistic with reconciliation · explicit branch-per-session | Multi-agent parallel work is impossible under a strict single-session lock |
| **OD-4** | `project/` location | Inside `.ai/project/` · at repository root · configurable | Inside `.ai/` is cleaner; at root is more discoverable to humans |
| **OD-5** | Session identity | Timestamp · content hash · host-provided ID | Host-provided IDs are not portable across models |
| **OD-6** | Approval expiry | Never · fixed period · on dependent-artifact change | Never-expiring approvals enable approval theatre (FM-9) |
| **OD-7** | Framework self-governance | Previous version · unversioned bootstrap · exempt | Determines how `core/` itself is developed and reviewed |
| **OD-8** | Human identity representation | Git identity · named role · both | Affects reviewer-independence checking in CI |
| **OD-9** | Ledger archive trigger | Size · time · lifecycle stage | Wrong trigger either breaches boot budget or archives prematurely |
| **OD-10** | Minimum viable install | Full 80 files · a reduced core for small projects | Full install may violate FM-1 on a two-week project |

---

## 17. Architecture Summary

| Property | Realisation |
|---|---|
| Repository as truth | 80 files; no state in model memory; conversation is not a record |
| Memory never trusted | Cold boot every session; B4 arithmetic reconciliation |
| Restartable | Session-as-transaction; STATE + ledger written atomically at close |
| Traceable | Append-only ledger; authority citation; hash-bound approvals |
| Documented workflow | 12 phases, 6 workflows, explicit entry/exit criteria |
| Freeze respected | Hash registry, CI-blocking, human-only thaw |
| AI assists only | Precedence rank 7; forbidden-action lists; LAW-12 stop conditions |
| Human approval | Approval-as-artifact with content-hash binding |
| Reproducible | Every output declares inputs, framework version, authority chain |
| Reusable | `core`/`project` partition with wholesale-replacement upgrade |
| Model-agnostic | Agents as contracts; adapter layer; LLM-free validation; 3,900-token boot |

**Deliverable of this document:** the complete architecture of AIEF 1.0.0 — 80 files across three partitions, 12 laws, 9 agent contracts, 6 workflows, 10 lifecycle stages, 10 templates, 7 schemas, 12 validation checks, 4 host adapters, 10 anticipated framework failure modes, and 10 open decisions requiring ratification.

**No framework file has been generated.** This is the architecture freeze candidate.
